data.message:
Don't say 'No more trains today' when the legacy shop failed

When the legacy shop failed, search() falls back to the new system's partial list. Its being empty after the
last departure no longer adds the 'No more trains today' notice; only the failure notice (which says the list may be
missing trains) is shown. The end-of-day notice still appears when the shop answered, and after the cut-off.

Tests: new test_a_failed_legacy_shop_after_the_last_train_doesnt_say_no_more_trains passes. Full offline suite:
694 passed, 15 skipped, 1 failed. The failure, test_cli_search_falls_back_with_exit_0 (tests/test_legacy.py), is
unrelated: it searches 2026-11-20, which the CLI rejects as in the past today (2026-11-21), before any search runs.

data.message:
Don't say 'No more trains today' after a failed legacy shop

When Renfe's legacy shop failed before the cut-off, the list came from the new system's partial timetable, so its having no train left proved nothing. search() still added 'No more trains today after HH:MM; try --date tomorrow.' next to the failure notice, and a script following it would give up on trains still to leave. That notice now appears only when the legacy shop answered.

Added test_a_failed_legacy_shop_never_says_no_more_trains (21:30 and 23:30, legacy 503): it failed on the base on the notice assertion and passes after the fix; it checks exit code 0. README updated to match.

Ran: uv run pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -rfE -> 695 passed, 15 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is tests/test_legacy.py::test_cli_search_falls_back_with_exit_0, which passes --date 2026-11-20; the CLI rejects it as in the past, so it fails before search runs, unrelated to this change. Not changed here.
